answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent identity to a costly, slow-to-build reputation garden: newcomers start with zero trust and must earn endorsements by completing verifiable work over time, like tending a garden rather than buying one overnight. A summit of established peers periodically audits new entrants, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means paying the same time and compute cost for each one, making a Sybil flood uneconomical while honest agents keep their standing.
